newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Generale des Eaux takes big stake in Havas.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Generale des Eaux takes big stake in Havas.

text.p: French group Generale des Eaux plans to sell its stake in pay televison group Canal Plus to Havas and take a 30 percent stake in Havas as part of a big French media industry shake-up.

According to a provisional draft of a company statement obtained by Reuters on Thursday, Generale des Eaux (CGE) will sell its 19.3 percent stake in Canal Plus to Havas for 5.6 billion francs ($1 billion) or 1,175 francs per share.
Generale des Eaux will also sell its Generale d'Images unit to Havas for 526 million francs.

In return, Generale des Eaux will receive shares to increase its stake in Havas to 20 percent from 2.1 percent currently. On top of that, it will buy a 10 percent stake from Alcatel Alsthom to bring its total stake in Havas to 30 percent.
Generale des Eaux will also sell its 10 percent stake in CanalSatellite to Canal Plus or to a third party designated by this company.
The cable activities of Generale des Eaux will be sold in the course of the year to "a partnership chosen in concertation with Havas and Canal Plus," the statement said.
A Generale des Eaux spokesman had no comment on the statement, provided by an industry source, and said a company board meeting was still going on.

"In a general context of strong growth in the audiovisual market, this agreement underlines the common wish of Generale des Eaux and Havas to create a big French communications and media group that will become one of the leaders in Europe," the statement said.

"It will allow Generale des Eaux to organise its 'Images' activities in a single and coherent entity, shouldered by a powerful partner and benefiting fully from the increasing synergies between Telecommunications and Images," the statement added.
Shares in Generale des Eaux and Havas were suspended ahead of a 1530 GMT news conference. Canal Plus traded 1.19 percent lower at 1,158 francs at 1200 GMT.
Havas has a market capitalisation of some 28 billion francs which would make Alcatel's 10 percent worth 2.8 billion.
The market capitalisation of Canal Plus, at Wednesday's prices,was also about 28 billion francs, while Generale des Eaux is worth 90 billion francs on the share market.

The increased Havas stake in Canal Plus will allow the French company, and indirectly Generale des Eaux, to remain the biggest shareholder in the merged group of Canal Plus and Dutch-based NetHold, controlled by Richemont and MIH.

It will also give Generale des Eaux a strong media "pillar" alongside its more traditional activities in water and services as well as its latest addition, the Cegetel telecommunications venture with Mannesmann AG, British Telecom Plc and SBC Communications Inc.
CGE will have a 45 to 50 percent stake in Cegetel which in turn owns mobile telecoms operator SFR, Cegetel long distance services and a unit for business services.

Next to that comes the 30 percent stake in Havas, which in turn owns 34.4 percent of Canal Plus, before the Nethold merger). It also holds 100 percent of publishing group CEP and the whole of Generale d'Images. Canal Plus owns 70 to 80 percent of digital satellite broadcaster CanalSatellite. ($ = 5.571 French Francs)
